all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Regulations on the establishment of firm pension schemes were relaxed in 1989, leading to increased competition among financial institutions for the management of these schemes and a tripling in the number of newly-established firm pension funds.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased competition in pension fund management can enhance the efficiency of capital allocation and improve the financial security of workers, thereby supporting economic growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The number of newly-established firm pension funds tripled in 1989.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reform significantly increased the number of pension funds, enhancing the retirement savings landscape in Japan, which is crucial for addressing the challenges of an aging population.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Regulations on the establishment of firm pension schemes were relaxed in 1989, covering smaller-sized firms, and the competition among financial institutions for the management of these schemes has increased.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on the relaxation of regulations for firm pension schemes, which does not relate to R&D funding or knowledge transfer, and lacks any indication of direct public R&D funding or innovation instruments.
